collections.prompt:
[DESIGN PROMPT]
[Flat standalone graphic artwork on a pure white background. The entire design sits as one island with a clear empty white margin of at least eight percent of the image on all four sides. Every paint drip stops in mid-air within about one letter-height, and no drip comes near the bottom margin.

A decaying undead bull elephant, stripped to bare bone, a warm ivory skull with the jaw hinged wide and a full set of teeth, the ribcage open and every joint articulated. Both tusks are whole, long and curved, and the trunk is intact. Seen in three-quarter view, heavily foreshortened toward the camera, and decayed asymmetrically so the two sides of the body do not match. Never drawn flat, never in clean side profile, never centred as a symmetrical emblem.

Layered over the beast as trophies taken off a beaten opponent, a cracked helmet punched through and snagged on its shoulder, a bent facemask cage clamped in its teeth, and a strip of torn cloth caught around one limb and dragging behind it. All of this taken gear is bare unpainted grey steel and grey cloth so it never competes with the colour of the beast.

The beast is driving straight at the viewer with its head dropped low, the weapons of the skull aimed at the camera and one forelimb tearing backward through the ground, with turf ripped up in long torn strips under it. Its eye sockets burn with acid green light.

Behind it and up to the right, well clear of the lettering so no character is covered, a towering wall of storm cloud with lightning forked through it, drawn as one flat shape in a single muted tone of cream at about half strength, the lower edge of that shape dissolving downward into long paint drips.

One text string only, on a single line across the bottom of the artwork:
ROLL TIDE
It contains only capital letters and single spaces. No apostrophe, no comma, no period, no punctuation mark of any kind.

Make that line enormous - the single largest element in the picture, spanning the full width of the artwork.

Set it in massive italic block capitals filled with crimson, wrapped in a thick black outline and a thin white keyline outside that, the baseline of the word torn into jagged shards, thick paint drips falling from the foot of every letter, the whole word resting on a ragged torn band of cream. One heavy black drop shadow, offset down and to the right.

Fill the empty space around the figure with paint splatters, long downward paint runs, torn jagged shard shapes, a rough airbrushed halo behind the body and fine speckled overspray.

Airbrushed sports-bar mural x 1980s heavy-metal album cover x drip-stencil street graffiti x trading-card hero pose.

Hold the whole picture to these values: crimson, cream, warm ivory bone, black as the darkest anchor, and acid green for the eye light alone. Repaint every object into that set. The single exemption is the taken gear, which stays neutral grey. The bone is warm ivory and never pure white.

Draw a visible black ink contour around every form, including the entire outer silhouette of the bone, so nothing dissolves into the white. Airbrush the gradients across the skull with hard specular hits on the brow and the cheekbone. Put a hard highlight along every top-facing edge and pool black shadow in every recess. Scuff and dry-brush the metal. Draw any chain link by individual link and any mesh as actual holes.

No mockup, no product photo, no garment shown, no hands holding it, no watermark, no signature, no border, no frame, no cropped artwork. No misspelled words and no lettering at all beyond the one string above - specifically the helmet carries no decal and no text, the facemask carries no text, every piece of cloth is blank and unmarked, the torn band under the word carries no second string, and there is no league shield anywhere. No background scenery, no landscape, no coloured backdrop, no rectangle or panel behind the artwork. No photorealistic human skin. No pumpkin, no bat, no cobweb, no gravestone and no candle anywhere in the picture.]

IMAGE ROLES:
- Image A = style/design reference only.
- Image B = actual tumbler mockup and must be preserved.

GOAL:
Create exactly 2 separate square mockup images using 1 single master design only.
Use the exact same design for both mockups. Do not create 2 different designs.

[OUTPUT SEPARATION & SAFETY]
- Output exactly 2 separate 1:1 images, generated independently. Never combine, collage, split-screen, overlap, or place both mockups in the same image.
- Keep any dark, horror, undead, or aggressive elements stylized and non-graphic. No gore, exposed wounds, or graphic bodily damage.

GENERAL RULES:
- Preserve Image B’s exact tumbler shape, proportions, handle, lid, straw, metallic rim, tapered lower body, and overall structure.
- Apply artwork only to the printable tumbler body.
- Do not print on the handle, lid, straw, or metallic rim.
- Keep all artwork fully inside the tumbler body silhouette.
- The print must follow the tumbler curvature naturally like a real full-wrap print.
- Use Image A only as inspiration for richness, premium collectible feel, color direction, texture, and overall style.
- Do not copy Image A literally.

DESIGN CONSISTENCY:
Use one single master design for:
- tumbler in Mockup 1
- box in Mockup 1
- tumbler in Mockup 2

Keep the same:
- main artwork
- typography
- color palette
- logos/badges
- decorative elements
- overall visual identity

3D / EMBOSSED LOOK:
Give the artwork a premium raised / embossed / dimensional look.
Keep it realistic and integrated into the surface.
Do not distort the tumbler shape.

MOCKUP 1:
Create a clean product mockup image showing:
- 1 tumbler based on Image B
- 1 matching product box placed with it

The box must look like a real premium retail box.
Use only the text/content already available in the DESIGN CONCEPT for the box layout.
Do not invent product specs, ingredients, components, or technical feature lists.
Keep the box text simple and realistic, like a real package, using only the provided design text.

MOCKUP 2:
Create a lifestyle image showing the same tumbler design as Mockup 1.
Keep the tumbler as the main focus.
Use a realistic lifestyle environment matching the niche.

VARIATION:
- Mockup 1 = product-focused image with tumbler + box
- Mockup 2 = lifestyle image
- Both must use the exact same design

BACKGROUND:
Use realistic, polished backgrounds that match the design concept and niche.
Keep the product as the hero.
Use believable lighting, reflections, depth, and contact shadows.

OUTPUT:
- Exactly 2 separate images
- 1:1 aspect ratio
- Same exact design in both images
- Mockup 1 = tumbler + matching box
- Mockup 2 = lifestyle image
- Premium, realistic, polished, e-commerce ready

OVERRIDE — NUMBER OF OUTPUTS (this rule wins over every rule above):

Only ONE product mockup image is attached to this message. Ignore any earlier
rule that says "1 mockup = 1 image", "3 mockups = 3 separate images", or that
ties the number of outputs to the number of uploaded mockups.

Generate EXACTLY 2 separate finished images from that single uploaded mockup.

- All 2 images must show the SAME product and keep the SAME core design
  concept, message, niche and visual identity.
- You may vary layout, composition, scale, placement and color balance slightly
  so each image still looks intentional — but it must stay the same design.
- Each of the 2 images must have a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT background scene:
  different location, angle, props, surfaces, staging and depth.
- Return 2 separate images. Never combine them into one collage, grid or
  contact sheet.

[Flat standalone graphic artwork on a pure white background. The entire design sits as one island with a clear empty white margin of at least eight percent of the image on all four sides. Every paint drip stops in mid-air within about one letter-height, and no drip comes near the bottom margin.

A decaying undead hawk, stripped to bare bone, a warm ivory skull with the beak held wide open, the ribcage bared and every joint articulated. The hooked beak and both sets of talons stay whole and sharp. Seen in three-quarter view, heavily foreshortened toward the camera, and decayed asymmetrically so the two sides of the body do not match. Never drawn flat, never in clean side profile, never centred as a symmetrical emblem.

Layered over the beast as trophies taken off a beaten opponent, a cracked helmet punched through and snagged on its shoulder, a bent facemask cage clamped in its teeth, and a strip of torn cloth caught around one limb and dragging behind it. All of this taken gear is bare unpainted grey steel and grey cloth so it never competes with the colour of the beast.

The beast is throwing its wings wide to the full width of the artwork, talons reaching out of the picture toward the viewer, head levelled at the camera, with turf ripped up in long torn strips under it. Its eye sockets burn with acid green light.

Behind it and up to the right, well clear of the lettering so no character is covered, a bank of four tall stadium floodlight towers burning at full blaze, drawn as one flat shape in a single muted tone of black at about half strength, the lower edge of that shape dissolving downward into long paint drips.

One text string only, on a single line across the bottom of the artwork:
GO HAWKS
It contains only capital letters and single spaces. No apostrophe, no comma, no period, no punctuation mark of any kind.

Make that line enormous - the single largest element in the picture, spanning the full width of the artwork.

Set it in massive italic block capitals filled with old gold, wrapped in a thick black outline and a thin white keyline outside that, the baseline of the word torn into jagged shards, thick paint drips falling from the foot of every letter, the whole word resting on a ragged torn band of black. One heavy black drop shadow, offset down and to the right.

Fill the empty space around the figure with paint splatters, long downward paint runs, torn jagged shard shapes, a rough airbrushed halo behind the body and fine speckled overspray.

Airbrushed sports-bar mural x 1980s heavy-metal album cover x drip-stencil street graffiti x trading-card hero pose.

Hold the whole picture to these values: old gold, warm ivory bone, black as the darkest anchor, and acid green for the eye light alone. Repaint every object into that set. The single exemption is the taken gear, which stays neutral grey. The bone is warm ivory and never pure white.

Draw a visible black ink contour around every form, including the entire outer silhouette of the bone, so nothing dissolves into the white. Airbrush the gradients across the skull with hard specular hits on the brow and the cheekbone. Put a hard highlight along every top-facing edge and pool black shadow in every recess. Scuff and dry-brush the metal. Draw any chain link by individual link and any mesh as actual holes.

No mockup, no product photo, no garment shown, no hands holding it, no watermark, no signature, no border, no frame, no cropped artwork. No misspelled words and no lettering at all beyond the one string above - specifically the helmet carries no decal and no text, the facemask carries no text, every piece of cloth is blank and unmarked, the torn band under the word carries no second string, and there is no league shield anywhere. No background scenery, no landscape, no coloured backdrop, no rectangle or panel behind the artwork. No photorealistic human skin. No pumpkin, no bat, no cobweb, no gravestone and no candle anywhere in the picture.]

IMAGE ROLES:
- Image A = style/design reference only.
- Image B = actual tumbler mockup and must be preserved.

GOAL:
Create exactly 2 separate square mockup images using 1 single master design only.
Use the exact same design for both mockups. Do not create 2 different designs.

[OUTPUT SEPARATION & SAFETY]
- Output exactly 2 separate 1:1 images, generated independently. Never combine, collage, split-screen, overlap, or place both mockups in the same image.
- Keep any dark, horror, undead, or aggressive elements stylized and non-graphic. No gore, exposed wounds, or graphic bodily damage.

GENERAL RULES:
- Preserve Image B’s exact tumbler shape, proportions, handle, lid, straw, metallic rim, tapered lower body, and overall structure.
- Apply artwork only to the printable tumbler body.
- Do not print on the handle, lid, straw, or metallic rim.
- Keep all artwork fully inside the tumbler body silhouette.
- The print must follow the tumbler curvature naturally like a real full-wrap print.
- Use Image A only as inspiration for richness, premium collectible feel, color direction, texture, and overall style.
- Do not copy Image A literally.

DESIGN CONSISTENCY:
Use one single master design for:
- tumbler in Mockup 1
- box in Mockup 1
- tumbler in Mockup 2

Keep the same:
- main artwork
- typography
- color palette
- logos/badges
- decorative elements
- overall visual identity

3D / EMBOSSED LOOK:
Give the artwork a premium raised / embossed / dimensional look.
Keep it realistic and integrated into the surface.
Do not distort the tumbler shape.

MOCKUP 1:
Create a clean product mockup image showing:
- 1 tumbler based on Image B
- 1 matching product box placed with it

The box must look like a real premium retail box.
Use only the text/content already available in the DESIGN CONCEPT for the box layout.
Do not invent product specs, ingredients, components, or technical feature lists.
Keep the box text simple and realistic, like a real package, using only the provided design text.

MOCKUP 2:
Create a lifestyle image showing the same tumbler design as Mockup 1.
Keep the tumbler as the main focus.
Use a realistic lifestyle environment matching the niche.

VARIATION:
- Mockup 1 = product-focused image with tumbler + box
- Mockup 2 = lifestyle image
- Both must use the exact same design

BACKGROUND:
Use realistic, polished backgrounds that match the design concept and niche.
Keep the product as the hero.
Use believable lighting, reflections, depth, and contact shadows.

OUTPUT:
- Exactly 2 separate images
- 1:1 aspect ratio
- Same exact design in both images
- Mockup 1 = tumbler + matching box
- Mockup 2 = lifestyle image
- Premium, realistic, polished, e-commerce ready

OVERRIDE — NUMBER OF OUTPUTS (this rule wins over every rule above):

Only ONE product mockup image is attached to this message. Ignore any earlier
rule that says "1 mockup = 1 image", "3 mockups = 3 separate images", or that
ties the number of outputs to the number of uploaded mockups.

Generate EXACTLY 2 separate finished images from that single uploaded mockup.

- All 2 images must show the SAME product and keep the SAME core design
  concept, message, niche and visual identity.
- You may vary layout, composition, scale, placement and color balance slightly
  so each image still looks intentional — but it must stay the same design.
- Each of the 2 images must have a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT background scene:
  different location, angle, props, surfaces, staging and depth.
- Return 2 separate images. Never combine them into one collage, grid or
  contact sheet.

[DESIGN PROMPT]
[Flat standalone graphic artwork on a pure white background. The entire design sits as one island with a clear empty white margin of at least eight percent of the image on all four sides. Every paint drip stops in mid-air within about one letter-height, and no drip comes near the bottom margin.

A decaying undead cougar, rotted away along one side only: one half still carries living hide with its markings whole and sharp, the other half is stripped to warm ivory bone with the ribs and the hinge of the jaw laid open. The living half keeps an unmarked unspotted tawny coat and the long heavy tail. Its remaining hide is painted in navy blue and silver grey, never the natural colour of the animal. Seen in three-quarter view, heavily foreshortened toward the camera, and decayed asymmetrically so the two sides of the body do not match. Never drawn flat, never in clean side profile, never centred as a symmetrical emblem.

Layered over the beast as trophies taken off a beaten opponent, a strip of torn cloth wrapped around its ribs and trailing from them, a broken facemask cage hooked over one limb, and a flattened helmet dragging from a chain at its neck. All of this taken gear is bare unpainted grey steel and grey cloth so it never competes with the colour of the beast.

The beast is driving straight at the viewer with its head dropped low, the weapons of the skull aimed at the camera and one forelimb tearing backward through the ground, with churned mud and broken chalk hash marks under it. Its eye sockets burn with acid green light.

Behind it and up to the right, well clear of the lettering so no character is covered, the flat silhouette of a huge open stadium bowl ringed with light masts, drawn as one flat shape in a single muted tone of silver grey at about half strength, the lower edge of that shape dissolving downward into long paint drips.

One text string only, on a single line across the bottom of the artwork:
RISE AND SHOUT
It contains only capital letters and single spaces. No apostrophe, no comma, no period, no punctuation mark of any kind.

Make that line enormous - the single largest element in the picture, spanning the full width of the artwork.

Set it in massive italic block capitals filled with navy blue, wrapped in a thick black outline and a thin white keyline outside that, the baseline of the word torn into jagged shards, thick paint drips falling from the foot of every letter, the whole word resting on a ragged torn band of silver grey. One heavy black drop shadow, offset down and to the right.

Fill the empty space around the figure with paint splatters, long downward paint runs, torn jagged shard shapes, a rough airbrushed halo behind the body and fine speckled overspray.

Airbrushed sports-bar mural x 1980s heavy-metal album cover x drip-stencil street graffiti x trading-card hero pose.

Hold the whole picture to these values: navy blue, silver grey, warm ivory bone, black as the darkest anchor, and acid green for the eye light alone. Repaint every object into that set. The single exemption is the taken gear, which stays neutral grey. The bone is warm ivory and never pure white.

Draw a visible black ink contour around every form, including the entire outer silhouette of the bone, so nothing dissolves into the white. Airbrush the gradients across the skull with hard specular hits on the brow and the cheekbone. Put a hard highlight along every top-facing edge and pool black shadow in every recess. Scuff and dry-brush the metal. Draw any chain link by individual link and any mesh as actual holes.

No mockup, no product photo, no garment shown, no hands holding it, no watermark, no signature, no border, no frame, no cropped artwork. No misspelled words and no lettering at all beyond the one string above - specifically the helmet carries no decal and no text, the facemask carries no text, every piece of cloth is blank and unmarked, the torn band under the word carries no second string, and there is no league shield anywhere. No background scenery, no landscape, no coloured backdrop, no rectangle or panel behind the artwork. No photorealistic human skin. No pumpkin, no bat, no cobweb, no gravestone and no candle anywhere in the picture.]

IMAGE ROLES:
- Image A = style/design reference only.
- Image B = actual tumbler mockup and must be preserved.

GOAL:
Create exactly 2 separate square mockup images using 1 single master design only.
Use the exact same design for both mockups. Do not create 2 different designs.

[OUTPUT SEPARATION & SAFETY]
- Output exactly 2 separate 1:1 images, generated independently. Never combine, collage, split-screen, overlap, or place both mockups in the same image.
- Keep any dark, horror, undead, or aggressive elements stylized and non-graphic. No gore, exposed wounds, or graphic bodily damage.

GENERAL RULES:
- Preserve Image B’s exact tumbler shape, proportions, handle, lid, straw, metallic rim, tapered lower body, and overall structure.
- Apply artwork only to the printable tumbler body.
- Do not print on the handle, lid, straw, or metallic rim.
- Keep all artwork fully inside the tumbler body silhouette.
- The print must follow the tumbler curvature naturally like a real full-wrap print.
- Use Image A only as inspiration for richness, premium collectible feel, color direction, texture, and overall style.
- Do not copy Image A literally.

DESIGN CONSISTENCY:
Use one single master design for:
- tumbler in Mockup 1
- box in Mockup 1
- tumbler in Mockup 2

Keep the same:
- main artwork
- typography
- color palette
- logos/badges
- decorative elements
- overall visual identity

3D / EMBOSSED LOOK:
Give the artwork a premium raised / embossed / dimensional look.
Keep it realistic and integrated into the surface.
Do not distort the tumbler shape.

MOCKUP 1:
Create a clean product mockup image showing:
- 1 tumbler based on Image B
- 1 matching product box placed with it

The box must look like a real premium retail box.
Use only the text/content already available in the DESIGN CONCEPT for the box layout.
Do not invent product specs, ingredients, components, or technical feature lists.
Keep the box text simple and realistic, like a real package, using only the provided design text.

MOCKUP 2:
Create a lifestyle image showing the same tumbler design as Mockup 1.
Keep the tumbler as the main focus.
Use a realistic lifestyle environment matching the niche.

VARIATION:
- Mockup 1 = product-focused image with tumbler + box
- Mockup 2 = lifestyle image
- Both must use the exact same design

BACKGROUND:
Use realistic, polished backgrounds that match the design concept and niche.
Keep the product as the hero.
Use believable lighting, reflections, depth, and contact shadows.

OUTPUT:
- Exactly 2 separate images
- 1:1 aspect ratio
- Same exact design in both images
- Mockup 1 = tumbler + matching box
- Mockup 2 = lifestyle image
- Premium, realistic, polished, e-commerce ready

OVERRIDE — NUMBER OF OUTPUTS (this rule wins over every rule above):

Only ONE product mockup image is attached to this message. Ignore any earlier
rule that says "1 mockup = 1 image", "3 mockups = 3 separate images", or that
ties the number of outputs to the number of uploaded mockups.

Generate EXACTLY 2 separate finished images from that single uploaded mockup.

- All 2 images must show the SAME product and keep the SAME core design
  concept, message, niche and visual identity.
- You may vary layout, composition, scale, placement and color balance slightly
  so each image still looks intentional — but it must stay the same design.
- Each of the 2 images must have a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT background scene:
  different location, angle, props, surfaces, staging and depth.
- Return 2 separate images. Never combine them into one collage, grid or
  contact sheet.

[Flat standalone graphic artwork on a pure white background. The entire design sits as one island with a clear empty white margin of at least eight percent of the image on all four sides. Every paint drip stops in mid-air within about one letter-height, and no drip comes near the bottom margin.

A decaying undead wolf, stripped to bare bone, a warm ivory skull with the jaw hinged wide and a full set of teeth, the ribcage open and every joint articulated. The long narrow muzzle stays whole with a full set of teeth and the ruff of the neck is still raised. Seen in three-quarter view, heavily foreshortened toward the camera, and decayed asymmetrically so the two sides of the body do not match. Never drawn flat, never in clean side profile, never centred as a symmetrical emblem.

Layered over the beast as trophies taken off a beaten opponent, a strip of torn cloth wrapped around its ribs and trailing from them, a broken facemask cage hooked over one limb, and a flattened helmet dragging from a chain at its neck. All of this taken gear is bare unpainted grey steel and grey cloth so it never competes with the colour of the beast.

The beast is driving straight at the viewer with its head dropped low, the weapons of the skull aimed at the camera and one forelimb tearing backward through the ground, with churned mud and broken chalk hash marks under it. Its eye sockets burn with acid green light.

Behind it and up to the right, well clear of the lettering so no character is covered, a full moon as one enormous flat disc, drawn as one flat shape in a single muted tone of cream at about half strength, the lower edge of that shape dissolving downward into long paint drips.

One text string only, on a single line across the bottom of the artwork:
GO PACK
It contains only capital letters and single spaces. No apostrophe, no comma, no period, no punctuation mark of any kind.

Make that line enormous - the single largest element in the picture, spanning the full width of the artwork.

Set it in massive italic block capitals filled with red, wrapped in a thick black outline and a thin white keyline outside that, the baseline of the word torn into jagged shards, thick paint drips falling from the foot of every letter, the whole word resting on a ragged torn band of cream. One heavy black drop shadow, offset down and to the right.

Fill the empty space around the figure with paint splatters, long downward paint runs, torn jagged shard shapes, a rough airbrushed halo behind the body and fine speckled overspray.

Airbrushed sports-bar mural x 1980s heavy-metal album cover x drip-stencil street graffiti x trading-card hero pose.

Hold the whole picture to these values: red, cream, warm ivory bone, black as the darkest anchor, and acid green for the eye light alone. Repaint every object into that set. The single exemption is the taken gear, which stays neutral grey. The bone is warm ivory and never pure white.

Draw a visible black ink contour around every form, including the entire outer silhouette of the bone, so nothing dissolves into the white. Airbrush the gradients across the skull with hard specular hits on the brow and the cheekbone. Put a hard highlight along every top-facing edge and pool black shadow in every recess. Scuff and dry-brush the metal. Draw any chain link by individual link and any mesh as actual holes.

No mockup, no product photo, no garment shown, no hands holding it, no watermark, no signature, no border, no frame, no cropped artwork. No misspelled words and no lettering at all beyond the one string above - specifically the helmet carries no decal and no text, the facemask carries no text, every piece of cloth is blank and unmarked, the torn band under the word carries no second string, and there is no league shield anywhere. No background scenery, no landscape, no coloured backdrop, no rectangle or panel behind the artwork. No photorealistic human skin. No pumpkin, no bat, no cobweb, no gravestone and no candle anywhere in the picture.]

IMAGE ROLES:
- Image A = style/design reference only.
- Image B = actual tumbler mockup and must be preserved.

GOAL:
Create exactly 2 separate square mockup images using 1 single master design only.
Use the exact same design for both mockups. Do not create 2 different designs.

[OUTPUT SEPARATION & SAFETY]
- Output exactly 2 separate 1:1 images, generated independently. Never combine, collage, split-screen, overlap, or place both mockups in the same image.
- Keep any dark, horror, undead, or aggressive elements stylized and non-graphic. No gore, exposed wounds, or graphic bodily damage.

GENERAL RULES:
- Preserve Image B’s exact tumbler shape, proportions, handle, lid, straw, metallic rim, tapered lower body, and overall structure.
- Apply artwork only to the printable tumbler body.
- Do not print on the handle, lid, straw, or metallic rim.
- Keep all artwork fully inside the tumbler body silhouette.
- The print must follow the tumbler curvature naturally like a real full-wrap print.
- Use Image A only as inspiration for richness, premium collectible feel, color direction, texture, and overall style.
- Do not copy Image A literally.

DESIGN CONSISTENCY:
Use one single master design for:
- tumbler in Mockup 1
- box in Mockup 1
- tumbler in Mockup 2

Keep the same:
- main artwork
- typography
- color palette
- logos/badges
- decorative elements
- overall visual identity

3D / EMBOSSED LOOK:
Give the artwork a premium raised / embossed / dimensional look.
Keep it realistic and integrated into the surface.
Do not distort the tumbler shape.

MOCKUP 1:
Create a clean product mockup image showing:
- 1 tumbler based on Image B
- 1 matching product box placed with it

The box must look like a real premium retail box.
Use only the text/content already available in the DESIGN CONCEPT for the box layout.
Do not invent product specs, ingredients, components, or technical feature lists.
Keep the box text simple and realistic, like a real package, using only the provided design text.

MOCKUP 2:
Create a lifestyle image showing the same tumbler design as Mockup 1.
Keep the tumbler as the main focus.
Use a realistic lifestyle environment matching the niche.

VARIATION:
- Mockup 1 = product-focused image with tumbler + box
- Mockup 2 = lifestyle image
- Both must use the exact same design

BACKGROUND:
Use realistic, polished backgrounds that match the design concept and niche.
Keep the product as the hero.
Use believable lighting, reflections, depth, and contact shadows.

OUTPUT:
- Exactly 2 separate images
- 1:1 aspect ratio
- Same exact design in both images
- Mockup 1 = tumbler + matching box
- Mockup 2 = lifestyle image
- Premium, realistic, polished, e-commerce ready

OVERRIDE — NUMBER OF OUTPUTS (this rule wins over every rule above):

Only ONE product mockup image is attached to this message. Ignore any earlier
rule that says "1 mockup = 1 image", "3 mockups = 3 separate images", or that
ties the number of outputs to the number of uploaded mockups.

Generate EXACTLY 2 separate finished images from that single uploaded mockup.

- All 2 images must show the SAME product and keep the SAME core design
  concept, message, niche and visual identity.
- You may vary layout, composition, scale, placement and color balance slightly
  so each image still looks intentional — but it must stay the same design.
- Each of the 2 images must have a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT background scene:
  different location, angle, props, surfaces, staging and depth.
- Return 2 separate images. Never combine them into one collage, grid or
  contact sheet.
